home.title: Put cancer under the microscope.
home.intro: Find what can slow cancer growth or harm cancer cells. Ask clear yes or no questions. Keep each answer tied to its test and source. A gap stays open.
home.head: Start with the question that matters to you.

choices.title: What can work against cancer?
choices.text: Start with a growth or cell death question. Read the finding and its proof. Then ask what test should come next.

choices.title: Is a skin mix safe?
choices.text: A drug crossing skin does not prove it reaches a tumor. The exact mix and your drugs need a check. Do not swallow comfrey powder.

choices.title: What about spike proteins?
choices.text: Spike is part of a virus. An infection is not the same as a shot. See what cancer claims can and cannot tell you.

choices.title: What should I ask my care team?
choices.text: Take the label and study link. Ask if tumors shrank, what harm occurred, and whether the product fits your care.

home.proof_title: What each type of proof can tell you.
home.proof_intro: A yes holds for the exact test. A no holds for the exact test too. A question with no sound answer stays open.

proof_steps.title: Cells in a lab
proof_steps.text: Can it change cells in a dish? Were healthy cells tested too?

proof_steps.title: Animals
proof_steps.text: Was it tested in mice? Did tumors shrink? Were there side effects?

proof_steps.title: People
proof_steps.text: Does the exact treatment help people, and what harm can it cause?

proof_steps.title: Compared with usual care
proof_steps.text: Were more people helped than harmed? Was usual care in the test too?

topics.name: Chemotherapy
topics.form: Named cancer drug regimens in human trials
topics.summary: The MPACT trial tested two cancer drugs against one drug in people with metastatic pancreas cancer. More people were alive with the two drugs at one and two years. The two-drug group also had more nerve and blood cell harm.
topics.research: The MPACT trial tested two cancer drugs against one drug in people with metastatic pancreas cancer. More people were alive with the two drugs at one and two years. The two-drug group also had more nerve and blood cell harm.
topics.human: Chemo benefit depends on the cancer, stage, drug plan and patient group. A survival rate after trial entry is not a cure rate or a forecast for one person.
topics.caution: Chemo can cause side effects. The risks can differ by drug and person. Ask the care team about your drug plan, blood counts, infection signs and lasting harm.
topics.next_step: Which trial matches the cancer, stage and drug plan? You can compare survival and harm at the same time point. Ask what the added drug changes versus the same care without it.

topics.question: Did adding nab-paclitaxel to gemcitabine improve survival in the MPACT pancreas trial?

study_details.heading: How chemotherapy works
study_details.text: Chemo drugs can kill cancer cells or stop their growth. The drugs can also harm healthy cells that grow fast. A treatment plan may aim for cure, lower return risk, slower growth or relief of symptoms.

study_details.heading: Cancer type and stage
study_details.text: MPACT tested adults with metastatic pancreas cancer. The cancer had spread to distant sites, which is stage IV. The trial did not test early-stage cancer or people with only local spread.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

study_details.heading: What it was compared with
study_details.text: The trial had 431 people assigned to nab-paclitaxel plus gemcitabine and 430 to gemcitabine alone. Both groups had chemotherapy. The comparison was an added drug, not chemo versus no cancer care.

study_details.heading: Survival at one and two years
study_details.text: At one year after random assignment, 35% were alive with the two drugs and 22% with one drug. The gap was 13 percentage points. At two years, the rates were 9% and 4%. Proof is in Table 2.

study_details.heading: Known side effects
study_details.text: NCI says chemo side effects can include fatigue, hair loss, nausea and mouth sores. Some drugs can cause blood cell loss, infection risk, bleeding, bowel changes and nerve harm. The effects can differ by drug. Not every person has every effect.

sources.label: Read the NCI side effect guide

study_details.heading: Lasting side effects
study_details.text: Some chemo effects can last after treatment. NCI names harm to the heart, lungs, nerves, kidneys and organs needed to have children. Some drugs can raise the risk of a second cancer years after treatment.

sources.label: Read the NCI side effect guide

study_details.heading: Side effect rates in MPACT
study_details.text: Serious nerve symptoms were in 17% with two drugs and 1% with one drug. Serious fatigue rates were 17% and 7%. Low infection-fighting blood cells were in 38% and 27%. The listed events are grade 3 or higher. Proof is in Table 3.

study_details.heading: Why one survival rate cannot cover all chemo
study_details.text: TAILORx tested early breast cancer with no spread to underarm lymph nodes. The cancers were hormone-sensitive and HER2-negative. The main compared group had a gene-test score from 11 to 25. A gene score is not a cancer stage.

study_details.heading: A different breast cancer result
study_details.text: At nine years, about 94% were alive in both TAILORx groups. The comparison was hormone therapy alone versus hormone therapy plus chemo after surgery. Most in the tested gene-score group had no added gain. Some women age 50 or younger had less return of cancer with chemo.

study_details.heading: What was read
study_details.text: The full MPACT and TAILORx papers were read, including methods, results, tables and discussion. A separate science reader has not checked these entries. The 2013 and 2018 results are dated trial results, not current rates for all patients.

expert_view.identity:
MPACT: Von Hoff et al. NEJM 2013;369:1691–1703. DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1304369; PMID 24131140; NCT00844649. Full primary paper read in PMC browser, 2026-10-14. Previously untreated metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, KPS ≥70; locally advanced disease excluded. ITT n=431 versus 430. Table 2: 12-month OS 35% (95% CI 30–39) versus 22% (18–27); p<0.001. 24-month OS 9% (6–13) versus 4% (2–7); p=0.02. Median OS 8.5 versus 6.7 months; HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.62–0.83). Grade ≥3 neuropathy 70/421 (17%) versus 3/402 (1%); fatigue 70/421 (17%) versus 27/402 (7%); neutropenia 153/405 (38%) versus 103/388 (27%). Different safety denominators retained. Quality of life not measured; open-label and sponsor-designed, analyzed and funded by Celgene. No head-to-head comparison with FOLFIRINOX.

TAILORx: Sparano et al. NEJM 2018;379:111–121. DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1804710; PMID 29860917; NCT00310180. Full primary paper read in PMC browser, 2026-10-14. HR-positive/HER2-negative, axillary node-negative early breast cancer; do not infer a uniform numbered stage. Randomized midrange score 11–25 analyzed n=6711: endocrine 3399 versus chemoendocrine 3312. Table 2: 9-year overall survival 93.9±0.5% versus 93.8±0.5% (Kaplan–Meier estimate ±SE). Primary invasive disease-free survival 83.3±0.9% versus 84.3±0.8%, HR 1.08 (95% CI 0.94–1.24), p=0.26. Overall survival secondary, HR 0.99, p=0.89. Nonadherence 11.8%; younger-age exploratory subgroup findings and possible ovarian suppression mechanism do not establish a universal no-benefit claim. Main-paper reading does not mean all supplementary appendices or an independent review have passed.

topics.name: Comfrey powder
topics.form: Powder from the plant and tested skin creams
topics.summary: The leaf extract group had fewer small early liver lesions in rats. The same group had more signs of liver cell injury. The test was of early lesions. Powder was not tested on an existing tumor. Proof is in Figure 1 and Tables 1 and 2.
topics.research: The leaf extract group had fewer small early liver lesions in rats. The same group had more signs of liver cell injury. The test was of early lesions. Powder was not tested on an existing tumor. Proof is in Figure 1 and Tables 1 and 2.
topics.human: The sources do not show a cancer benefit in people. Some skin creams have a use for sprains and bruises.
topics.caution: Raw powder is not a tested skin cream. Drying the plant does not prove its poisons are gone.
topics.next_step: Can a defined powder change an existing tumor without liver harm? The extract test does not answer that. The powder question stays Open.
topics.question: Does a DMSO mix of this powder slow tumor growth?

expert_view.identity:
Full paper read. Ethanolic leaf extract by mouth in a chemically induced early-lesion model. Twenty rats per group initially; only eight control and nine treated survivors analyzed. Deaths excluded, severe attrition and unclear randomization. Fewer small lesions with more megalocytic/vacuolated hepatocytes. Not an established-tumor or powder/DMSO skin test.

Review: Second AI source audit complete, 2026-10-14; independent scientific reader and replication open

Matching product/tumor question: Open.

study_details.heading: Cancer type and stage
study_details.text: The full study tested rats with early liver lesions. Those lesions are not a human stage I, II, III or IV cancer. The study did not test treatment of an established human tumor.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

study_details.heading: What was tested
study_details.text: The full study used a leaf extract by mouth in rats with early liver lesions. Early lesions are changed tissue spots before established tumors. The test did not use powder with DMSO on skin.

study_details.heading: What it was compared with
study_details.text: The control rats had water. Each group started with twenty rats. Only eight control rats and nine extract rats were left in the final check. Deaths were left out of that check.

study_details.heading: What changed
study_details.text: Some small lesions were fewer with the extract. The study also had more signs of liver cell injury. Less early damage in one count does not prove less cancer or healthy liver cells.

study_details.heading: How it may work
study_details.text: The extract was linked to less cell division. The same study had injured liver cells. The cause of each change needs a separate test.

study_details.heading: What is still open
study_details.text: Many rats were lost before the final check. The study does not answer whether comfrey powder with DMSO treats a tumor. That exact mix stays Open.

study_details.heading: What was read
study_details.text: The full extract paper was read. The older long-term feeding paper was not read in full. A separate science reader has not checked the finding.

study_details.heading: Survival in people
study_details.text: The rat study did not measure human survival. Deaths and losses in a rat test cannot give a human survival percentage.

topics.question: Did injected DMSO slow breast-tumor growth in this mouse test?

expert_view.identity:
Tested form: DMSO in saline, injected into mice with 4T1 tumors

Cancer model: Female BALB/c mice with subcutaneous 4T1 breast tumors; five per group

Comparison: Saline injections without DMSO

Endpoint: Tumor volume over time and final tumor weight

Proof: S-067; Figure 1: 1 mg/g growth difference days 13–19, p<0.01; n=5/group. Daily intraperitoneal DMSO for 10 days. The 0.25 mg/g group had no significant tumor-weight benefit. Small, short mouse experiment; macrophage findings do not prove a causal human mechanism.

Read level: full primary paper; methods, results, figures and discussion

Review: Second AI source audit complete, 2026-10-14; independent scientific reader and replication open

topics.name: Spike proteins
topics.form: Isolated SARS-CoV-2 spike protein preparation, not virus or vaccine
topics.summary: Cell colony counts were lower with the spike sample than with the control. A colony is a group of cells that grows from a cell. Counts were about half of the control. Proof is in Figure 1. Only one prostate-cell line was tested.
topics.research: Cell colony counts were lower with the spike sample than with the control. A colony is a group of cells that grows from a cell. Counts were about half of the control. Proof is in Figure 1. Only one prostate-cell line was tested.
topics.human: The study was not a vaccine or infection test. The result does not show that a shot treats or causes cancer.
topics.caution: COVID can be serious during cancer care. Ask the team about shot timing, infection risk, and new symptoms.
topics.next_step: Can a new team repeat the result with clear sample checks? Benefit in people, other cells and vaccine effects stay Open.

Tested form: Isolated SARS-CoV-2 spike protein preparation, not virus or vaccine

Read level: full primary paper; methods, results, figures and discussion

topics.summary: The cell test signal was lower with the drug in two breast cell lines. The test used estrogen, a hormone. Proof is in Figure 2. The 2026 paper is from a different team. The older mouse paper still has a journal concern.
topics.research: The cell test signal was lower with the drug in two breast cell lines. The test used estrogen, a hormone. Proof is in Figure 2. The 2026 paper is from a different team. The older mouse paper still has a journal concern.
topics.human: Benefit in people stays Open. This cell result does not fix the flaws in the earlier mouse study. A trial listing alone does not show benefit.
topics.caution: Human and animal products are different. A cancer use needs a trial or a treating clinician, not a home dose.
topics.next_step: Can a new team repeat the cell test? Can people safely reach the drug level used? Human benefit and the disputed mouse result stay Open.
topics.question: Did ivermectin lower the cell-viability signal in these breast-cell tests?

expert_view.identity:
Tested form: Research ivermectin in cultured cells

Cancer model: MCF-7 and T-47D estrogen-stimulated breast cancer cell lines

Comparison: Same estrogen conditions with 0.01% DMSO vehicle and no ivermectin

Endpoint: MTT viability after five days

Proof: S-070; Rujimongkon et al., 2026, Figure 2A–B: 3 and 5 µM ivermectin reduced estrogen-stimulated MTT signal in MCF-7 and T-47D; 10 nM estradiol, five days, n=3 independent experiments; two-way ANOVA. This is viability/metabolic signal, not tumor survival. Micromolar exposure and human delivery are unresolved. Combination analysis elsewhere reuses the same team’s 2025 data; not independent replication.

Read level: full primary paper; methods, results, figures and discussion

Review: Second AI source audit complete, 2026-10-14; independent scientific reader and replication open

Original broad question: Did the exact tested form reduce cancer growth against a comparison group?. Wider product and human benefit remains Open.

study_details.heading: Cancer type and stage
study_details.text: The cancer finding comes from cells or animals. No human cancer stage was tested for this finding. A cell line or mouse tumor does not prove an effect at human stage I, II, III or IV.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

study_details.heading: What was tested
study_details.text: Two breast cancer cell lines had estrogen, a hormone, with ivermectin for five days. The study ran three separate tests. The 2026 study is from a different team.

study_details.heading: What it was compared with
study_details.text: The control cells had the same hormone and solvent with no ivermectin. The test measured a signal from living cells.

study_details.heading: What changed
study_details.text: The cell test signal was lower with ivermectin in both cell lines. The signal shows cell activity. The signal is not a direct cell count or a test of how long people live. Proof is in Figure 2A and 2B.

study_details.heading: How it may work
study_details.text: Some hormone and growth signals changed. The study does not prove which signal caused the lower cell test result. Some drug-resistant cells had different results.

study_details.heading: What is still open
study_details.text: Can people safely reach the drug levels used in these cell tests? Human cancer benefit stays Open. The older mouse paper still has a journal concern. This study does not settle that concern.

study_details.heading: What was read
study_details.text: The full 2026 paper was read. The journal concern on the older mouse paper was also read. A separate science reader has not checked the finding.

study_details.heading: Survival in people
study_details.text: The cell and mouse findings do not measure how long people live. No human survival rate is known from those tests.

topics.name: Hydroxychloroquine
topics.form: Hydroxychloroquine added to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel
topics.summary: No gain in length of life was shown. At one year, 41% were alive with the added drug and 49% with cancer drugs alone. Tumor response was higher with the added drug. A tumor response is not the same as longer life. Proof is in the short study report and Figures 2 and 3.
topics.research: No gain in length of life was shown. At one year, 41% were alive with the added drug and 49% with cancer drugs alone. Tumor response was higher with the added drug. A tumor response is not the same as longer life. Proof is in the short study report and Figures 2 and 3.
topics.human: The trial was in people with pancreatic cancer. More tumors responded, but the main survival goal was not met. The drug can also cause harm.
topics.caution: Heart rhythm and eye risks need a medical check. Do not start this drug for cancer on your own.
topics.next_step: Could a chosen group of people gain a benefit? Full methods and a second check stay Open. This No is for length of life in this trial.
topics.question: Did added hydroxychloroquine show better one-year survival in this pancreatic-cancer trial?

expert_view.identity:
Tested form: Hydroxychloroquine added to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel

Cancer model: 112 untreated advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer patients; randomized 55 versus 57

Comparison: The same chemotherapy without hydroxychloroquine

Endpoint: Overall survival at 12 months; primary endpoint

Read level: primary structured abstract and figure legends read; full-text access blocked; ORR secondary p=0.047

Check date: 2026-10-14

Review: Primary source readback; second scientific review open

12-month OS 41% versus 49%; secondary ORR 38.2% versus 21.1%, p=0.047

Original broad question: Did the exact tested form reduce cancer growth against a comparison group? Broad product and human scope remains Open.

study_details.heading: Cancer type and stage
study_details.text: The trial was in people with advanced or metastatic pancreas cancer. Metastatic means spread to distant sites, which is stage IV. The abstract does not give a separate survival result for each stage.

sources.label: Read how cancer stage is defined

study_details.heading: What was tested
study_details.text: The trial had 112 people with advanced pancreas cancer. Fifty-five had added hydroxychloroquine with cancer drugs. Fifty-seven had the same cancer drugs alone.

study_details.heading: What changed
study_details.text: At one year, 41% were alive with the added drug and 49% with cancer drugs alone. No clear survival gain was shown. A separate tumor response result was higher with the added drug.

study_details.heading: Why the results differ
study_details.text: Tumor response means a measured change in a tumor. Survival means how long people live. A gain in tumor response does not prove longer life.

study_details.heading: What was read
study_details.text: The primary abstract and figure notes were read. Full-paper access was blocked. The full methods and a separate science check remain Open.

study_details.heading: Survival in people
study_details.text: At twelve months after trial entry, 41% were alive with added hydroxychloroquine and 49% with the same cancer drugs alone. The trial had 55 and 57 people in those groups. The rates are for the trial groups, not a personal forecast.

lessons.title: Spike proteins: what you need to know
lessons.intro: This lesson is about the spike on SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19.

sections.heading: What is spike?
sections.text: Spike is a protein on the virus surface. It helps the virus enter a cell. Spike is not the whole virus. A lab test of spike is not the same as a test of infection.

sections.heading: Why do vaccines use it?
sections.text: COVID shots help immune cells learn to spot spike. An mRNA shot has instructions to make a spike target. The mRNA is broken down by the body. A protein shot has the target itself. These shots do not contain a live COVID virus.

sections.heading: Do COVID-19 vaccines cause cancer?
sections.text: NCI reports no evidence that COVID-19 shots cause cancer, make it return, or make it grow. A cell test alone does not prove those claims in people. NCI is the U.S. National Cancer Institute.

sections.heading: What did the isolated spike test show?
sections.text: A 2022 lab test had fewer groups of prostate cancer cells with a spike sample. The groups are called colonies. The study used one cell line. The test was not of a shot or infection. Benefit in people stays Open.

sections.heading: What did the infection study show?
sections.text: A 2025 study used mice with sleeping breast-cancer cells in the lungs. Cell growth was seen after flu or COVID infection. Human records linked COVID with cancer deaths and lung spread of breast cancer. Those links do not prove cause. The study did not test a shot or spike alone.

sources.label: Read the infection and cancer study

sections.heading: Can one alarming paper settle it?
sections.text: A 2021 paper about spike and DNA repair was retracted in 2022. The paper was withdrawn by the journal. DNA is the cell's gene code. The paper is not sound proof that COVID shots cause cancer.

sections.heading: What is useful during cancer care?
sections.text: Ask the team about infection risk and shot timing. A shot can swell lymph nodes, small glands that help fight germs. The swelling can affect some scans. Tell the scan team when and where you had the shot. New or lasting swelling needs a check.

sections.heading: Are there vaccine risks?
sections.text: Sore arms and fever can occur. Rare serious effects, including heart inflammation, are tracked. Your risks and care plan matter. Ask for current advice for your age and health, not a fixed schedule from this page.

lessons.title: Can less sugar starve cancer?
lessons.intro: Food choices can affect health. They are not a simple way to turn off a tumor.

sections.heading: What is known?
sections.text: Cancer cells use sugar, but so do healthy cells. NCI says no studies show that stopping sugar makes a cancer shrink or disappear. A healthy eating plan can help you get through care.

sections.heading: What can you do?
sections.text: Ask for food advice that fits your weight, symptoms, and treatment. Do not cut out whole food groups based only on a cancer slogan.

sources.label: Read the food and supplements guide

lessons.title: Why the exact product matters
lessons.intro: A food is not the same as an oil or a lab extract. Each form needs its own test.

sections.heading: Do forms share the same proof?
sections.text: A lab extract result does not prove that food or skin oil works the same way. The tested dose and route can differ. Use the study for the form that was tested.

sections.heading: What should you bring to a review?
sections.text: You should bring the label and study link. Tell the team what dose you use. Ask if it can affect your drugs, surgery, or tests. A natural label does not prove safety.

sources.label: Read the guide to herbs during care

lessons.title: Does more oxygen mean less cancer?
lessons.intro: Can more oxygen help? A lab test is not proof that a drink can treat cancer.

sections.heading: What does the research mean?
sections.text: Low oxygen can change tumor growth or drug response. This lab link does not mean that a drink will help. Tests in cells and tests in people are not the same.

sections.heading: What is the clear caution?
sections.text: Do not drink or inject peroxide for cancer. The liquid can burn the gut and cause dangerous gas bubbles. Call Poison Control if you swallow it. You should get advice right away.

questions.heading: What is the exact question?
questions.text: Ask one yes or no question at a time.

questions.heading: What was tested?
questions.text: Name the form, cancer model, and test conditions.

questions.heading: What was the comparison?
questions.text: Name the groups in the test. How did their results differ?

questions.heading: What was measured?
questions.text: Keep cell death, tumor growth, pain, and length of life as distinct results.

questions.heading: Where is the proof?
questions.text: Link the source. Record the test results. Did a new group get the same result?

questions.heading: What is still open?
questions.text: Keep gaps open. No proof is not a no. Ask what test comes next.
